We need to propose a retrosynthesis route using templates 1914393, 1914394, 1914395 in this order. The target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1.

We applied template 1914393 to target, got a pair: product? Actually apply_template returns possible retrosynthetic disconnections: It gave a tuple of two SMILES: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'). So applying template 1914393 splits target into two fragments: fragment A: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (the core without the side chain) and fragment B: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 (the side chain with a CCl substituent). Good.

Now we need to apply template 1914394 to each fragment? The order is 1914393 then 1914394 then 1914395. Likely we apply 1914394 to each of the fragments sequentially. We attempted applying 1914394 to fragment A, got no result. So maybe apply to fragment B. We did that, got result: ('ClCCl', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'). So fragment B further disconnections: yields ClCCl (dichloromethane?) and FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 (a simpler side chain lacking the CCl aromatic). Good.

Now we need to apply template 1914395 to the remaining fragments (maybe the aromatic core and the simplified side chain). Let's apply 1914395 to fragment A (COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1).
